forum.author: Fleuve

scraped_replies.html:
Hello ​@Fleuve 

The WeAct BlackPill is not an official ST product.

ST resources support genuine ST products. ST does not guarantee that clones or counterfeit products operate correctly with the firmware that ST provides.

Thank you for your understanding.

If work with this board must continue, use one of the ST USB CDC host examples as a comparison with the project and check for any differences.
BR
Gyessine
scraped_replies.author: Gyessine

scraped_replies.html:
As ​@Gyessine said, the Black Pill is not an ST Product, and might not have a genuine STM32.

 

Therefore it would be best to first get this working on a genuine ST board:

https://www.st.com/en/microcontrollers-microprocessors/stm32f411ce.html#tools-software

Once you’ve got it working on a genuine ST board, you could then move on to the Black Pill

 

Note that connecting to USB via flying leads is not going to give great results;  you’d be better using a board with a dedicated USB host socket - looks like the 32F411EDISCOVERY is the best bet for that ...

scraped_replies.html:
​@Fleuve 

 I prototype everything on a breadboard

Breadboards aren’t great for high-speed digital circuits - such as USB.

You will be far better off using a dev board with known-good USB hardware.

 

NUCLEO-F411RE with its STM32F411RET6 chip could do the trick

It does not have any hardware for the microcontroller’s USB.

As previously noted, the 32F411EDISCOVERY would be far more appropriate ...

scraped_replies.author: Fleuve

scraped_replies.html:
Thanks to everyone for every pointed direction. I finally succeeded after figuring out a few mistakes. First, at the beginning, I only had my engraver as a device to test my host. Application_Ready started triggering ON after I decided to create my own device using a BluePill. Next, I had assumed that my USB_OTG_FS_VBUS (PA9) would power my VBUS. But in reality, PA9 and VBUS must be powered by a 5-volt source.



Then, the callback name is USBH_CDC_ReceiveCallback, and the while (1) loop looks like this

 

 while (1)
  {
    /* USER CODE END WHILE */
    MX_USB_HOST_Process();

    if (Appli_state == APPLICATION_READY && !Once)
    {
    	HAL_UART_Printf(huart2, "Application Ready V2
");

    	HAL_UART_Printf(huart2, "Sending Homing
");
    	USBH_StatusTypeDef Result;
    	Result = USBH_CDC_Transmit(&hUsbHostFS, (uint8_t*)"$h
", 6);

    	HAL_UART_Printf(huart2, "Transmit Home Result : %d
", Result);
    	USBH_CDC_Receive(&hUsbHostFS, CDC_RX_Buffer, sizeof(CDC_RX_Buffer));
    	Once = 1;
    }
}

The rest is identical to the introduction. 
 

After that, I was back to square one with my laser engraver. Application_Ready still wasn’t triggering. After modifying USBH_CDC_InterfaceInit

 

extern UART_HandleTypeDef huart2;
static USBH_StatusTypeDef USBH_CDC_InterfaceInit(USBH_HandleTypeDef *phost)
{

  USBH_StatusTypeDef status;
  uint8_t interface;
  CDC_HandleTypeDef *CDC_Handle;

  for (int i = 0; i < USBH_MAX_NUM_INTERFACES; i++)
  {
	  HAL_UART_Printf(huart2, "IF=%d CLASS=%02X SUB=%02X PROT=%02X
",
             i,
             phost->device.CfgDesc.Itf_Desc[i].bInterfaceClass,
             phost->device.CfgDesc.Itf_Desc[i].bInterfaceSubClass,
             phost->device.CfgDesc.Itf_Desc[i].bInterfaceProtocol);
  }

  interface = USBH_FindInterface(phost, COMMUNICATION_INTERFACE_CLASS_CODE, ABSTRACT_CONTROL_MODEL, COMMON_AT_COMMAND);

I discovered that Creality was using protocol 0x00 instead of 0x01. So I modified usbh_cdc.h
 

#define COMMON_AT_COMMAND                                       0x00U

Now this method is compatible with the Nucleo-STM32F411RE, and pins PA11 and PA12 are populated. I’m even thinking of modifying my breadboard and making the Nucleo the central processor with a custom 40-pin female header board @ DIP 40.
